thread:
Marcus Lin: Need quick security scope review on the internal “assignment debug” endpoint we’re adding for route experiments (PR-28596). Goal is oncall/support can hit an endpoint and get an explanation of *why* request landed in variant X (hash inputs, selected variant, config version).

Marcus Lin: Questions:
1) do we expose via Console backend only, or also directly on router service?
2) RBAC gating: what permission string / role? (support vs eng)
3) redaction: what do we need to strip / hash?

Jordan Lee: TL;DR we built it in the policy engine service behind `/internal/experiments/assignment_debug` (not the data plane router). It takes route_id + stickiness_key + optional headers and returns computed bucket + variant_id + evaluator version.

Jordan Lee: It’s super useful for skew debugging (missing sticky key, low entropy, etc). But agree: cannot be public.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: +1 to “not on router”. If it’s on data plane it’s going to be harder to reason about blast radius + more paths where it could leak.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: For gating: we already have RBAC in Console backend for experiments mutations. My suggestion:
- endpoint only reachable via Console backend (server-to-server)
- require `experiments.debug:read` permission
- default allow only `platform-oncall`, `support-tier3`, `security-admin` roles

Kaitlyn Nguyen: If we *must* keep a direct service endpoint for SREs, put it behind mTLS + allowlist + separate “break-glass” token, but I’d rather not for beta.

Sean Gallagher: SRE take: we need something during incidents where Console is down / auth is broken. But also, we can live with “Console backend only” if we have an internal curl path that uses the same auth.

Sean Gallagher: What I don’t want is a debug endpoint that can be invoked from customer VPCs. For Private deployments, this needs to be disabled or only accessible from customer admins (and even then… careful).

Benji Okafor: Current implementation assumes Redwood control plane. It’s not wired into Private package yet. We can add an explicit config guard: `debug_endpoints_enabled=false` by default in private deployments.

Chloe Martin: From Console backend side we can proxy it (like our existing “policy explain” tooling) and keep the actual service endpoint on a private network. That way no public ingress. Also easier to add rate limiting + audit.

Dylan Brooks: Agree with proxy via Console backend. Support uses Console most of the time anyway.

Marcus Lin: ok, RBAC-wise: `experiments.debug:read` sounds right. Are we ok letting support-tier3 use it? They’ll be the ones fielding “why am I on variant B?” tickets.

Kevin Osei: If support gets it, we need strong audit log coverage. At minimum: actor, account_id, route_id, experiment_id (if provided), and reason/comment if we have it. Also retention needs to match enterprise expectations (our audit export pipeline).

Rafael Mendes: Also add the runbook link in the response? Even just a “see runbook” pointer would be helpful when oncall is stressed.

Jordan Lee: Re redaction: please do NOT accept raw headers as input. We only need a stable stickiness key + route_id + maybe customer/account id.

Jordan Lee: If folks start pasting full request headers we’ll inevitably leak `Authorization` / cookies / internal routing headers into logs.

Chloe Martin: +1000. I can make the API accept a minimal payload:
- `account_id`
- `route_id`
- `stickiness_key` (string)
- optional `seed` override? (but we probably shouldn’t)
- optional `request_id` (if we want to look up captured attrs)

Chloe Martin: And response should NOT echo `stickiness_key` back. It can show `stickiness_key_hash=sha256(...)`.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: +1. Also ensure we never log request body / prompts. If someone provides request_id, any join should pull only the assignment context fields (no prompt, no tool args).

Sean Gallagher: Another thing: response can include config version + “config fetched at” timestamp, but don’t include full config blob. Too easy to leak internal routing policy details.

Benji Okafor: currently it returns `experiment_config_etag` + `config_version` and a small “decision trace” string. I can adjust to:
- `decision_trace` limited to fixed fields (hash inputs types, precedence path)
- max length 4KB
- no raw inputs

Marcus Lin: Can we also make sure we don’t accidentally create a data exfil path between tenants? e.g. someone uses account A creds but supplies account B route_id.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: Yes, Console backend must validate that `account_id` matches the caller’s tenant scope. Same check as other experiment APIs.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: I want the debug endpoint to require BOTH:
- authz check on caller
- tenant scoping check on target account

Rafael Mendes: Rate limits: please. Incidents get spammy. Suggest 60 rpm per actor, burst 10.

Sean Gallagher: And add a metric for usage + denied requests. We’ve been burned by “internal” endpoints becoming noisy.

Jordan Lee: One nuance: sometimes missing stickiness key means we fall back to default key (we recently fixed skew issues here). For debug, we should explicitly show which stickiness key source was used, but in a redacted way.

Jordan Lee: e.g. `stickiness_source=explicit|customer_id|ip_hash|random` (whatever precedence is). That helps explain skew without leaking the actual value.

Chloe Martin: That’s doable.

SecurityBot: Automated review checklist for new debug endpoints:
- [ ] No public ingress route
- [ ] RBAC permission added + tested
- [ ] Tenant scoping enforced
- [ ] No sensitive values echoed (Authorization, cookies, prompt text, raw stickiness keys)
- [ ] Access logged + exportable
- [ ] Rate limiting enabled

Marcus Lin: :thumbsup: on checklist.

Kevin Osei: For access logging, please make sure the audit event includes `action=experiments.assignment_debug.read` and includes a `target` field (route_id + experiment_id if resolved). We can wire to SIEM export.

Dylan Brooks: What about UX? Support asked if they can copy/paste the “variant header” from customer reports.

Chloe Martin: We can accept `x-redwood-experiment-id` + `x-redwood-variant-id` as optional inputs, but again: only those IDs, not the full header set.

Jordan Lee: That’s safe.

Sean Gallagher: Last ask: make sure it’s disabled by default in prod until we’re confident. Feature flag / allowlist for internal accounts.

Marcus Lin: Plan:
- ship behind feature flag `route_experiments_debug_endpoint`
- only enabled for Redwood internal accounts + beta allowlist
- Console backend proxy only
- RBAC `experiments.debug:read`
- redaction: hash stickiness key, don’t accept raw headers, don’t return config blob
- audit log event + rate limit

Marcus Lin: I’ll add these requirements as PR comments + follow-up task. Any objections?

Kaitlyn Nguyen: None. Please add an integration test for “cannot debug other tenant” + “support-tier3 allowed / tier1 denied”.

Rafael Mendes: :+1: and I’ll update the oncall runbook to include the new flow once it’s live.

Sean Gallagher: Works. Ping me when ready; we’ll do a quick game day to verify it’s not reachable from outside.

Jordan Lee: Sounds good. I’ll update the decision trace fields and remove anything that’s too verbose.

Marcus Lin: Done, thanks all.
